First off, this admittedly may not have been the best place to have brought this up. That said, Internet discussions do end up going off on tangents, and that's where I went off to.

But, that aside, my original point regarded the comment that "voting with your wallet works." In the more generalized case, it can have some VERY serious flaws. The way that it was phrased implied, at least to me, that doing so is a panacea, and if only people would realize that not purchasing is an effective means of communication. I disagreed, because, while this CAN be effective, my personal experience is that often a company will simply cancel a product rather than change it to be more to the liking of the consumer. Hence the analogy, "cure the disease by killing the patient."

Not-so-ironically the NFL is likely a case where this WILL work. As it is the NFL, their product is inherently going to be football, so if people are no longer consuming that product because of this, they are much more incentivized to change it rather than doing what many other companies would and cancel the product outright.
